Static assets stay:
/brand/...
/_next/...

CHILD-SIMPLE VERSION:
Everything you use after entering the school starts with `/app`. The login desk and plumbing do not.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. TARGET ROUTE TREE — NEXT.JS NATIVE
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Preferred conceptual App Router tree:

src/app/
├── layout.tsx
├── page.tsx                         # public Learners Area welcome / intro
├── login/
├── register/
├── reset-password/
├── onboarding/
├── pending/
├── app/
│   ├── layout.tsx                   # ACTIVE USER gate, no ordinary shell chrome
│   │
│   ├── (shell)/
│   │   ├── layout.tsx               # Sidebar + Topbar + main scroll container
│   │   ├── page.tsx                 # /app = Dashboard
│   │   ├── listening/
│   │   ├── reading/
│   │   ├── writing/
│   │   ├── speaking/
│   │   ├── grammar/
│   │   ├── vocabulary/
│   │   ├── mocks/
│   │   ├── progress/
│   │   ├── assignments/
│   │   ├── live-classes/
│   │   ├── video-lessons/
│   │   ├── courses/
│   │   ├── coach/
│   │   ├── notifications/
│   │   ├── support/
│   │   ├── management/
│   │   ├── teacher/
│   │   ├── admin/
│   │   └── owner/
│   │
│   └── (focus)/
│       ├── layout.tsx               # full-viewport minimal assessment shell
│       ├── listening/...
│       ├── reading/...
│       ├── writing/...
│       ├── mocks/...
│       └── other approved focus surfaces
│
└── api/                             # UNCHANGED URL namespace

Route groups `(shell)` and `(focus)` must not appear in the URL.

The outer `/app/layout.tsx` owns:
- session existence;
- current DB user read;
- account-status/admission gate;
- locale/theme context if appropriate;
- private noindex intent.

The shell layout owns:
- desktop rail;
- topbar;
- mobile drawer;
- content viewport;
- utilities.

The focus layout owns:
- full viewport;
- safe Back/Exit;
- optional compact assessment utilities;
- no ordinary sidebar/topbar.

Never duplicate authentication logic across every migrated page if the common `/app` gate can enforce it safely.
Domain and role authorization still remains server-side at the service/page/API boundary.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. DO NOT BUILD A FAKE SPA
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Booster's static reference can switch visible panels in one document.
Learners Area must NOT copy that implementation pattern.

Learners Area already uses Next.js App Router.
Keep:
- real URLs;
- deep links;
- server components;
- server authorization;
- route-level streaming where useful;
- normal browser history;
- Next `<Link>`;
- `router.push/replace`;
- route groups/layout persistence.

The app-like feeling must come from:
- persistent layouts;
- local tap feedback;
- prefetching;
- route-specific data boundaries;
- avoiding unnecessary loading fallbacks;
- small client bundles;
- stable shell;
- responsive state;
- correctly scoped caching.

Not from:
- hiding/showing every page in one DOM;
- `onclick="go(...)"`;
- manual `pushState` replacing Next;
- giant initial HTML;
- giant global JavaScript state.

CHILD-SIMPLE VERSION:
Use real rooms with doors and addresses. Do not paint every room on one giant wall and hide them with curtains.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. CURRENT LEARNERS AREA STRENGTHS — PRESERVE
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The current product already contains major systems that must survive the `/app` conversion:

- server-side current-user reload;
- role hierarchy;
- account-status/admission gate;
- PostgreSQL source of truth;
- private R2/S3 resource model;
- upload intent/finalize lifecycle;
- publication states;
- audit log;
- current Sidebar/Topbar shell;
- independent shell scroll containers;
- responsive mobile drawer;
- Day/Night;
- EN/UZ;
- global search;
- notifications;

- route performance diagnostics;
- focus-entry infrastructure;
- dedicated Listening focus route architecture;
- Reading attempts;
- Writing workspaces;
- Speaking banks/practice;
- RIWI/Coach;
- Dictionary/canonical lexical architecture;
- assignments;
- mock/progress surfaces;
- admin/teacher/owner boundaries;
- extensive unit/UI/database QA.

A route namespace migration that regresses any of these is a failure.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. APP CONVERSION SUCCESS DEFINITION
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Success is NOT:
- adding `/app` to one URL;
- creating a redirect;
- moving Dashboard only;
- adding a PWA manifest;
- changing Sidebar links;
- renaming a route group.

Success means:
1. every authenticated product page has one canonical `/app...` address;
2. all internal navigation generates canonical `/app...` links;
3. old private URLs safely redirect;
4. cold reload works on every canonical route;
5. browser Back/Forward works;
6. role authorization remains server-authoritative;
7. focus assessments remain full-screen;
8. shell pages share one persistent shell;
9. APIs remain stable;
10. stored links and notifications do not break;
11. module state/query parameters survive;
12. performance does not regress;
13. SEO/robots exclude private app pages;
14. public root/intro/auth flow remains correct;
15. all role surfaces work;
16. all four IELTS sections and supporting modules work;
17. Content OS from Master Prompts 1/2 remains integrated;
18. RIWI remains secure and functional;
19. no legacy private URL becomes the primary route;
20. no independently solvable P0/P1 product gap remains hidden.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
10. PUBLIC ENTRY FLOW
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Target entry flow:

                               ┌───────────────┐
                               │      /        │
                               │ intro/welcome │
                               └───────┬───────┘
                                       │
                    ┌──────────────────┼──────────────────┐
                    │                  │                  │
                 no user          active user        restricted
                    │                  │                  │
                    ▼                  ▼                  ▼
                /login              /app              /pending

Rules:
- Approved desktop intro video remains only at the public root.
- Direct `/app/...` deep links never replay the intro.
- Mobile/touch welcome behavior remains as approved unless current repository truth has since changed.
- Root CTA destination must become `/app` for an active authorized user.
- Root must not leak private user data.
- Landing canonical metadata remains public only.
- Private `/app` routes remain `noindex`.
- Logged-in active users may still intentionally visit `/`; the root behavior must be deterministic and tested.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
11. AUTHENTICATION BOUNDARY
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Preserve the current secure architecture.

The Booster reference uses client-side bearer state and revalidation.
DO NOT copy that.

Learners Area requirements:
- existing secure session cookie remains authoritative at transport/session level;
- middleware performs only coarse session presence where appropriate;
- `/app` layout reloads current user/role/status from PostgreSQL;
- APIs independently authorize;
- role is never trusted from the client;
- account status is never trusted from the cookie alone;
- suspended/rejected/pending behavior remains explicit;
- logout remains server-side and clears the session;
- open redirect protections remain.

Moving pages beneath `/app` must simplify coarse route protection, not weaken it.

Suggested coarse protected paths:
- `/app`
- account lifecycle paths that already require a session, if still outside app.

Do not treat middleware as the final authorization layer.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
12. SAFE `next` / RETURN-TO-DESTINATION MIGRATION
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Audit every flow that stores or passes an internal destination:

- login `next=`;
- registration continuation;
- Google auth state/callback;
- Telegram auth callback;
- reset flow if applicable;
- logout/re-entry;
- onboarding completion;
- pending approval continuation;
- desktop intro destination;
- notification href;
- global search result href;
- support/report context path;
- teacher/admin links;
- stored lesson/resource links;
- emails/messages if the repo creates them.

Requirements:
- default signed-in destination becomes `/app`;
- legacy `/dashboard` next values translate to `/app`;
- legacy private `/reading?...` translates to `/app/reading?...`;
- query strings are preserved;
- fragments are preserved only where safe and supported;
- external origins are rejected;
- protocol-relative URLs are rejected;
- `javascript:` and malformed destinations are rejected;
- role-invalid destinations fall back safely.

Do not create an open redirect while migrating route prefixes.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
13. CANONICAL ROUTE BUILDER
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Create or formalize one typed, dependency-light route helper for canonical app URLs.

Conceptual examples:

appHref.home()
appHref.listening()
appHref.listeningTest(id)
appHref.reading()
appHref.readingAttempt(id)
appHref.writing()
appHref.speaking()
appHref.mock(id)
appHref.adminListening(id)
appHref.teacherStudent(id)

Exact API is an implementation decision.

Goals:
- eliminate duplicated hard-coded private path strings;
- make future SAT/course additions predictable;
- make redirects/search/breadcrumbs/notifications use the same canonical path rules;
- work in both server and client code;
- contain no secret;
- contain no authorization decision.

Do NOT centralize actual access control into a client-safe path helper.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
14. LEGACY PATH COMPATIBILITY
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Old private URLs will exist in:
- browser bookmarks;
- old chat messages;
- stored notification hrefs;
- teacher messages;
- screenshots/docs;
- search indexes in local browser history;
- internal test fixtures.

Do not 404 them immediately.

Create a compatibility layer.

Example mapping:
`/dashboard` -> `/app`
`/listening` -> `/app/listening`
`/reading?tab=retention` -> `/app/reading?tab=retention`
`/writing/exam/<id>` -> `/app/writing/exam/<id>`
`/owner/audit` -> `/app/owner/audit`

Requirements:
- preserve query parameters;
- preserve dynamic path parameters;
- avoid redirect loops;
- old API routes do NOT redirect;
- old public auth routes do NOT redirect into `/app`;
- unauthorized users still go through auth;
- use 308 permanent redirects only after canonical routing is stable;
- during staged development, temporary redirects may be safer.

Every old route must be classified:
REDIRECT
PUBLIC-STAYS
API-STAYS
STATIC-STAYS
REMOVED-WITH-REASON.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
15. PHYSICAL ROUTE MIGRATION
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Prefer physical Next route ownership under `src/app/app/...`.

Do not rely on permanent rewrites that make the browser show an old path while rendering new app code.

Use `git mv` where practical so history remains understandable.

Migration rule:
- canonical code lives under `/app`;
- legacy files become minimal redirect shims or are removed after redirect configuration is proven;
- never maintain two full copies of the same page;
- no double business logic;
- no duplicate layouts.

After each route family move:
- typecheck;
- focused route tests;
- cold reload;
- client navigation;
- old-route redirect;
- role access.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Target:

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│                 │ TOPBAR                                           │

└─────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Desktop:
- sidebar is its own scroll container;
- main content is its own scroll container;
- document itself should not become the accidental scrolling surface.

Mobile:
- no permanent sidebar width;
- drawer or approved compact navigation;
- full main width;
- safe-area support.

Preserve the current fixed viewport shell principles (`h-dvh`, `min-h-0`, scoped overflow) unless better measured evidence justifies change.

Do not infer staff mode from a mutable localStorage flag.

- narrow layouts must not wrap into unusable height;

Do not add decorative controls merely to resemble Booster.

21. GLOBAL SEARCH AFTER `/app` MIGRATION

- Reading;

- Vocabulary;
- Live classes;
- lessons/materials;
- future content OS entities.

- authorization is rechecked server-side;
- no unpublished/unauthorized content leak;
- search opens fast;
- debounce behavior remains measured;
- query state does not become part of sensitive telemetry;
- selecting a result navigates via Next;
- focus route result gets correct `/app/...` focus path;
- old stored hrefs are canonicalized before rendering.

Regression test:
No search result href for a private page starts with a legacy top-level private prefix.

Do not blindly rewrite historical rows without inspection.

B. reviewed migration;
C. both, when appropriate.

Requirements:
- new notifications store canonical `/app` paths;
- existing legacy private hrefs resolve to canonical paths;
- external hrefs remain governed by existing policy;
- malformed hrefs do not become open redirects;
- role-forbidden destinations do not bypass authorization;
- notification history remains readable.

Audit all database columns or JSON payloads that may store internal routes.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
23. BREADCRUMBS AND PARENT NAVIGATION
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/app/writing/history
/app/speaking/ai
/app/admin/listening
/app/owner/audit

Rules:
- longest-prefix behavior remains correct;
- dynamic paths get meaningful parents;
- Dashboard `/app` has no fake Back;
- a direct deep link always has a safe parent;
- browser history may be used when it truly returns within the app, but fallback href remains canonical;
- filters/scroll should survive normal history back where possible.

No breadcrumb should display the literal word `app` to the learner unless product copy explicitly wants it.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
24. INSTANT INTERACTION — KEEP NEXT NATIVE
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Preserve the existing local-first interaction principle.

User should see response to a tap quickly:
- pressed/pending state;
- route intent;
- local tab switch where genuinely local;
- skeleton only where useful;
- previous content may remain until next route is ready if that measures better.

Do not:
- add a blanket route-level loading screen that triggers the historical ~300ms fallback delay;
- replace Next router;
- prefetch every large route indiscriminately;
- hide failed requests behind endless spinners.

Update route-key classification to understand `/app/...`.

Performance diagnostics must use fixed workspace names, never raw IDs/query text.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
25. BROWSER HISTORY
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Every meaningful app location must have a real URL.

Required:
- hard reload works;
- Back works;
- Forward works;
- opening in a new tab works;
- copying URL works;
- filters with URL state survive;
- module tabs that are intended shareable remain encoded;
- focus attempts remain deep-link safe subject to auth/ownership;
- browser history is not manually replaced by a parallel routing system.

Booster's app-like panel transitions are a UX reference.
Learners Area retains superior deep-link semantics.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

- Back/Forward work;
- unauthorized direct access is denied server-side;

Gap-closure requirements:
- inventory current routes/components/APIs/tests before edits;
- identify legacy placeholders, dead controls, NotMigrated states, hard-coded sample data, or stale route strings;
- close every repository-solvable P0/P1 defect discovered in this module;
- classify external/provider/content blockers honestly;
- add regression tests for every defect fixed.

CHILD-SIMPLE VERSION: Dashboard moves into the `/app` school building without losing its books, scores, history, or rules.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
48. FOCUS ROUTE ARCHITECTURE
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The normal shell and assessment focus mode must be structurally separate.

Target conceptual rule:

/app/listening                     -> shell
/app/listening/tests/<id>          -> focus
/app/listening/attempts/<id>       -> focus

/app/reading                       -> shell
/app/reading/attempts/<id>         -> focus when current Reading exam UX requires it

/app/writing                       -> shell
/app/writing/exam/<id>             -> focus if formal exam mode

/app/mocks                         -> shell
/app/mocks/<id>/attempt/...        -> focus

Focus mode must:
- retain authentication;
- retain account-status gate;
- retain ownership/publication checks;
- fill the viewport;
- remove ordinary sidebar/topbar;
- expose a safe top-left Back/Exit;
- use normal Learners Area button geometry;
- support mobile safe areas;
- never trap the learner;
- keep timer/save/submit accessible;
- preserve deep links;
- restore normal shell on exit.

Do not rely on hiding shell with fragile CSS if route layouts can express the architecture correctly.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
49. FOCUS MODE VS USER-TOGGLED FOCUS
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
There are two concepts:

A. STRUCTURAL ASSESSMENT FOCUS
- route belongs to `(focus)`;
- shell chrome is not rendered;
- used for formal or purpose-built work.

B. USER-TOGGLED SHELL FOCUS
- ordinary shell route;
- user presses Focus;
- sidebar/nonessential chrome hides;
- user can exit.

Do not conflate them.

A Listening full test can be structural focus.
A vocabulary list can remain shell mode with optional user focus.
A management screen should not offer learner focus.

Audit current `ShellUtilities`, `TestFocusEntry`, and route groups after migration.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
50. WEB APP MANIFEST — APP-LIKE ENTRY, NOT A NATIVE APP
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The user asked for a `/app` web system, not a native mobile app.

Booster reference includes a web manifest with an app start URL and standalone display.
Learners Area may safely adopt the concept if it improves the product.

Recommended manifest:
- name = Learners Area;
- short_name from brand config;
- start_url = `/app`;
- id = `/app` where supported;
- scope = `/` unless a narrower scope can safely handle login redirects;
- display = `standalone`;
- theme/background colors from Learners Area design tokens;
- icons from approved brand derivatives;
- EN/UZ metadata where platform support permits.

Do NOT:
- copy Booster manifest values;
- add a service worker only to say "PWA";
- cache private authenticated HTML/API responses offline without a threat model;
- cache sensitive assessment answers/audio/transcripts in a shared worker cache.

Manifest/installability is supplementary.
Canonical `/app` routing is the primary goal.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
51. SERVICE WORKER POLICY
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Default decision:
NO service worker for private learning data unless a measured product requirement justifies one.

If one already exists by the time this prompt runs:
- audit it;
- ensure it cannot serve another user's private content;
- ensure logout invalidates private cache;
- ensure stale answer keys cannot leak;
- ensure API writes are not replayed unexpectedly;
- ensure offline mode is truthful.

If no service worker exists:
do not create one merely to imitate Booster.

The application may still have a manifest and standalone display behavior without inventing unsafe offline caching.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
52. ROOT METADATA / ROBOTS / SITEMAP
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Public root:
- indexable only according to current product policy;
- correct canonical URL;
- Learners Area metadata.

Private `/app`:
- noindex, nofollow, nocache intent;
- excluded from sitemap;
- never expose dynamic private IDs through public sitemap generation.

APIs:
- not sitemap content.

Preview:
- remains noindex.

Audit `robots.ts`, `sitemap.ts`, root metadata, `/app` metadata inheritance and preview environment behavior.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
53. THEME AND LANGUAGE UNDER `/app`
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Preserve server-resolved first-paint theme.
No light-mode flash for Night users.

Preserve EN/UZ.

Requirements:
- `/app` route moves must not reset locale/theme cookies;
- hard reload deep inside `/app` keeps theme/locale;
- focus routes inherit correct theme;
- management inherits correct theme;
- auth/public routes remain consistent;
- all new labels exist in both dictionaries;
- no raw English server error code appears in UZ UI;
- no hard-coded user-facing route names bypass dictionaries.

Theme and locale are UI settings, not learning progress.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
54. BRAND AND INTRO ASSETS
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

App shell:

The `/app` conversion is not a rebrand.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
55. BUTTON / CONTROL CONSISTENCY
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The user has repeatedly reported accidental square/rectangle controls and inconsistent Listening tabs.

The `/app` migration must not reintroduce this class of regression.

Define/retain canonical primitives:
- primary button;
- secondary button;
- ghost button;
- icon button;
- tab;
- pill/badge;
- destructive action;
- link-inline;
- card CTA.

Rules:
- active tab is not automatically a primary CTA;
- button radius/height follow design tokens;
- no browser-default buttons;
- no duplicate conflicting global CSS for the same component state;
- no `!important` chains used to patch architecture;
- focus-visible state is clear;
- 44px-class touch targets where applicable.

Add visual/DOM regression tests for shared controls.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
56. GLOBAL CSS AND STYLE BOUNDARIES
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Audit `globals.css` during migration.

Goals:
- remove route-specific duplicate rules that conflict;
- prefer component classes/tokens;
- scope focus-surface styles;
- avoid selectors that accidentally style every `[aria-pressed=true]` button;
- avoid styling based on old pathname DOM assumptions;
- preserve Day/Night variables;
- preserve responsive shell breakpoints.

Any global rule added must answer:
1. Which components need it?
2. Could it affect another module?
3. Is a component class safer?
4. Is there already a conflicting rule?

Run a static duplicate-selector audit if practical.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
57. CONTENT OS INTEGRATION — MASTER PROMPTS 1/2 ARE AUTHORITATIVE

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
59. COURSE EXPANSION — `/app` MUST NOT BE IELTS-LOCKED
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

`/app/courses/ielts`

`/app/courses/<course>`

But current primary module routes may remain concise:
`/app/listening`
`/app/reading`
etc.

Do not prematurely force every current route to `/app/courses/ielts/...` unless product evidence supports that complexity.

Separate:
- global app namespace;
- course-specific content model.

Future course addition must not require rebuilding auth, shell, assets, publication, assignments, audit, or app routing.

- cross-route Back links.

Do not move the separate Dictionary repository into this app repository.
Preserve release/integration boundary.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
62. API NAMESPACE — STAYS `/api`
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This is an absolute invariant.

Do NOT transform:
/api/reading/...
into
/app/api/reading/...

Do NOT create a duplicate proxy API namespace.

Why:
- APIs are not pages;
- existing clients/tests depend on them;
- middleware origin checks are built around `/api`;
- moving them gives no user benefit;
- it increases regression risk.

Page migration may require APIs to return new canonical page hrefs.
The endpoint paths themselves stay stable unless a separate API migration is justified.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
63. RESOURCE DELIVERY — STAYS OUTSIDE `/app`
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Private object delivery remains through the approved resource/storage architecture.

Do not make:
/app/resources/<key>
a public static-file shortcut.

Keep server authorization before private resource access.

Signed/private media URLs remain bounded.

`/app` route conversion must not:
- expose R2 object keys unnecessarily;
- make bucket public;
- convert private media to static assets;
- break Range/media delivery;
- break audio/video playback because relative paths changed.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
64. R2 / STORAGE AFTER CONTENT OS
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Preserve the final accepted storage transport from the Listening/content migration.

Reverify:
- upload intent;
- direct presigned PUT if that is the accepted final architecture;
- exact Content-Type signing;
- CORS;
- finalize HEAD verification;
- claim/attachment;
- private reads;
- cleanup;
- ownership.

`/app` must not change storage signing hosts/paths.
Page paths are unrelated to object signature paths.

Test from the actual `/app` origin after deployment because CORS AllowedOrigins may need the stable Preview and Production origins.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
65. DATABASE — ROUTE MIGRATION SHOULD NOT FORCE DATA REWRITE
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A URL namespace change should not require destructive learning-data migration.

Prefer route canonicalization at application boundaries.

Database migrations are justified only if:
- canonical route/href storage model truly needs a schema change;
- Content OS integration requires it;
- an existing accepted migration is pending.

Do not rewrite:
- attempts;
- grades;
- transcripts;
- lexical records;
- content IDs;
- RIWI evaluations;
- audit history

merely because page URLs gained `/app`.

If stored internal hrefs need migration:
- dry run first;
- count affected rows;
- preserve external URLs;
- idempotent update;
- backup/safety point;
- verify.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
66. SERVER COMPONENT / CLIENT COMPONENT BOUNDARY
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Preserve Next.js strengths.

Server by default for:
- auth gate;
- role/status;
- database reads;
- content summaries;
- publication rules;
- static page structure.

Client only where interaction requires:
- recorder;
- timers that need live UI;
- local tab state;
- text inputs/autosave;
- media controls;
- menus/dialogs;
- browser speech recognition;
- upload progress.

Do not mark entire `/app` layout `use client`.

Do not ship owner/admin code into every student route if route boundaries can avoid it.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
67. DATA FETCHING
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Audit each route for:
- sequential independent queries;
- N+1 query patterns;
- duplicated current-user reads;
- waterfall fetches;
- loading behavior.

Parallelize independent server reads.

Keep authorization before sensitive data.

Do not move private server data fetching to the browser merely to mimic an SPA.

Use Suspense only when it improves measurable UX.
No blanket fallback that creates a 300ms perceived stall.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
68. ROUTE-LEVEL ERROR BOUNDARIES
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Every critical app region must fail truthfully.

Use:
- segment `error.tsx` where appropriate;
- existing RegionFailureNotice for isolated data regions;
- retry;
- localized user message;
- correlation ID only where safe.

Do not:
- turn DB schema mismatch into fake empty content;
- swallow 500 and show "0 items";
- leave infinite pending;
- expose raw SQL/server stack;
- redirect every error to Dashboard.

Focus assessments need an escape/back path even when the inner data fails.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
69. LOADING STATES
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Define loading ownership:

Navigation:
- immediate link pending acknowledgement;
- keep stable shell;
- avoid full-app white flash.

Data region:
- scoped skeleton if operation is meaningfully delayed.

Mutation:
- disable duplicate submit where appropriate;
- visible pending;
- visible success/failure;
- release in `finally`.

Upload:
- real byte progress only;
- no fake percentage.

AI evaluation:
- explicit bounded progress stage;
- no invented completion.

Every pending state must terminate.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
70. PREFETCH POLICY
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Use Next prefetch and existing intent-prefetch intentionally.

Do prefetch:
- likely next lightweight module route when beneficial;
- links where the framework default is already efficient.

Do not aggressively prefetch:
- huge assessment payloads;
- owner/admin pages for students;
- answer-key-bearing review data;
- media files;
- every route in the sidebar on mobile data;
- RIWI provider actions.

Measure before adding custom prefetch complexity.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

73. MIDDLEWARE MIGRATION
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Update coarse protected-page matching carefully.

Target simplification:
- protect `/app` as the private application namespace;
- preserve session-required account lifecycle routes outside `/app` if needed;
- retain `/api` origin checking;
- retain CSP/security headers on all routes.

Do not:
- remove DB-backed page/API authorization;
- trust middleware role claim as current truth;
- forget focus routes because they also begin `/app`;

- break Listening authored sandbox CSP endpoint under `/api`.

suspended /app

CSP on /app and public pages.

74. CSP / SECURITY HEADERS

Do not relax CSP to fix routing.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

If a student copies it:

If an admin returns to `/app/listening`:
- learning shell returns.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
79. LANDING INTRO PERFORMANCE
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The root intro video must not slow normal app navigation.

Rules:
- `/app` never downloads intro video solely because it exists at `/`;
- brand intro component stays in root bundle boundary;
- preload only where intended;
- timeout/fallback remains;
- media query prevents waste on unsupported touch/mobile contexts according to approved behavior;
- app route chunks do not import intro video component.

Measure root and /app separately.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
80. APP SHELL PERFORMANCE BUDGET
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Establish a measured baseline before migration.

Targets are budgets, not unsupported claims:
- local visible acknowledgement: <= ~100 ms where feasible;
- warm module navigation meaningful content: target <= 500 ms in local production-mode lab;
- production p95 target <= ~1.5 s for ordinary shell navigation, measured later;
- no recurring 5–10 second dead interaction;
- no accidental 300 ms blanket fallback tax;
- no route imports heavy editor/recorder code until needed.

Compare BEFORE vs AFTER on same machine.
Document environment and sample size.
Do not call lab numbers production numbers.

- pagination.

Legacy redirect must preserve valid query.

Canonical app navigation must not drop query unexpectedly.

Back/Forward must restore intended state.

Reject/normalize invalid query values using existing domain rules.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
123. HASH / ANCHOR PRESERVATION
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
If any current deep links use fragments:
- inspect them;
- preserve when safe through client navigation;
- do not depend on server redirects preserving behavior without testing;
- avoid using hash as hidden authentication state.

If no meaningful private fragment routes exist:
do not invent them.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
124. REVALIDATION PATHS
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Search:
`revalidatePath(`
and related cache invalidation.

Update page paths to canonical `/app/...` where page cache/revalidation uses route strings.

APIs stay `/api`.

Do not leave mutations revalidating dead legacy routes while canonical pages stay stale.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
125. REDIRECT() CALLS
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Search every `redirect()`.

Classify:
- auth;
- role;
- default module;
- legacy alias;
- content state;
- not-found alternative.

Update private destinations to `/app`.

Test redirect loops:
`/` -> /app -> /login -> ... must terminate correctly.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
126. ROUTER.PUSH / ROUTER.REPLACE
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Search client navigation.

Update:
- `router.push`;
- `router.replace`;
- hard-coded `window.location`;
- `location.assign/replace`;
- `<a href>` internal links.

Prefer Next navigation for same-origin app routes.
Keep real external links native.

Do not convert downloads or external providers to router navigation.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
127. FORM ACTIONS
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Audit form actions and post-submit redirects.

Examples:
- auth forms;
- support;
- content management;
- profile;
- imports;
- assignments.

Successful mutation should return/navigate to canonical `/app` destination where applicable.

Do not let old route action attribute survive hidden in server-rendered forms.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
If application sends or generates internal links:
- support responses;
- password/auth messages;

- exported reports.

Historical messages may still contain old URLs; compatibility redirects must keep them working.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
129. STUDENT EXPORTS
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Student data export may include paths/labels.

Audit:
- PDFs;
- text/JSON export;

Do not expose private signed URLs.

Use canonical public base URL plus `/app` only when a navigable link is actually needed.

130. ROUTE CONSTANT DRIFT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Currently route knowledge may live in:

- breadcrumbs;

- middleware;

- notifications.

Reduce avoidable duplication.

Possible architecture:

- authorization remains separate;
- domain focus route checks may derive from the manifest if safe.

Do not create a god-object containing auth/database logic.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
131. ACTIVE NAV ITEM
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

132. APP HOME / DASHBOARD URL
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Preferred:

If `/app/dashboard` must temporarily exist:

- redirect the other;
- links use only canonical.

The prompt recommends `/app` as canonical Home.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
133. PUBLIC `/dashboard` DEPRECATION
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Old `/dashboard` is a legacy private URL.

Final behavior:
- signed-out -> login with safe continuation to `/app`;
- active -> redirect `/app`;
- restricted -> existing account-state rules.

No full Dashboard implementation remains at `/dashboard`.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
134. ONBOARDING / PENDING
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
These are account-state surfaces, not normal learning modules.

Preferred:
- remain outside ordinary `/app` shell;

Reasons:
- pending user should not see app navigation they cannot use;
- onboarding may need simplified chrome;
- auth lifecycle remains clearer.

However all destinations from these flows must end at `/app` once access is active.

Document final decision.

`/app`.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
136. PROFILE / LOGOUT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Logout:
- server-side endpoint;
- current session invalidated;

Profile menu:

- no self-role editing;
- mobile usable.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
143. MIGRATION STRATEGY — ROUTES FIRST, DELETE LATER
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Safe sequence:

1. build canonical route helper;
2. add `/app` root layout/gates;
3. move/copy low-risk shell pages;
4. update nav/breadcrumbs/search;
5. migrate module route families;
6. migrate focus routes;
7. migrate role management routes;
8. update stored-href boundaries;
9. add legacy redirects;
10. static sweep;
11. browser QA;
12. only then delete obsolete duplicate implementations.

Never delete the old route before the new route is verified.
Never keep duplicate live implementations after acceptance.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
144. GIT DISCIPLINE
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Logical commits.

Example:
1. refactor(nav): add canonical app route helpers
2. feat(app): add authenticated /app shell
3. refactor(routes): move learner hubs under /app
4. refactor(focus): move assessment routes under /app
5. refactor(management): move staff/admin/owner under /app
6. fix(links): canonicalize internal hrefs and redirects
7. feat(webapp): add manifest start_url /app if approved
8. test(app): route/role/history regression matrix
9. docs(app): final architecture and migration ledger

Do not force these exact commits if change boundaries differ.
Do not create one giant 50k-line commit.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
145. NO AUTOMATIC MAIN MERGE
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Final task branch only.

At completion:
- push;
- verify remote SHA;
- report;
- do not merge main;
- do not delete source branches unless owner asks.

If PR is needed:
prepare it, do not merge automatically.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
146. DRIZZLE MIGRATION POLICY
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A pure route move ideally needs zero DB schema migrations.

If Master Prompt 1/2 or integration work adds migrations:
- preserve journal order;
- generate through repository workflow;
- fresh PGlite/PostgreSQL where required;
- populated upgrade;
- no db:push in release acceptance;
- no fake down migration;
- no Production apply.

Report pending Preview/Production actions explicitly.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
147. SHARED PREVIEW DATABASE
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Do not apply new shared Preview migrations merely to test routing.

Use isolated Preview where authorized for destructive/high-risk work.

If the final app requires shared Preview migration:
- identify exact database;
- exact pending range;
- safety point;
- backup/PITR receipt;
- owner approval;
- apply only authorized range.

Routing work itself should be independently testable on isolated data.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
148. BACKUP / RESTORE
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Preserve RIWI owner decisions and operational policy.

No route migration should claim backup/PITR success.

If final release acceptance includes restore drill:
- read-only inspect source;
- restore to isolated destination;
- measure;
- verify app integrity;
- never restore over Production;
- delete/quarantine isolated restore according to policy.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
App routes do not change retention policy.

Preserve accepted:
- RIWI conversation retention;
- Speaking audio/transcript retention;

- legal/safety hold semantics;
- cleanup.

Do not accidentally prevent cleanup because stored route prefix changed.

RIWI/provider outbound DTO minimization remains.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

- correct answers;

unless architecture already safely requires server-side hidden data.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
153. ROLE CHANGE DURING SESSION
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Current DB role/status is authoritative.

Scenario:

Next protected request must reflect current role.

Do not keep client-cached role as authorization truth in the persistent shell.

The shell may display cached-looking UI only if server authorization still protects every action.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
154. ACCOUNT SUSPENSION DURING SESSION
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Scenario:
student has `/app/reading` open.
Account becomes suspended.

Next server navigation/API write must deny according to policy.

Persistent shell cannot create a permanent authorization window.

Test direct API and page refresh.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
155. PUBLICATION CHANGE DURING SESSION
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Scenario:
student browses published content.
Admin archives it before new attempt start.

Starting new attempt must obey current publication rules.

Historical permitted attempt review follows historical rules.

Route migration must not bypass publication checks by rendering stale shell state.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
156. CACHE SAFETY
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Private user-specific data must not be shared between users.

- Dashboard;
- attempts;

- notifications;
- RIWI;
- admin.

Public immutable brand assets can cache.

Canonical content may use carefully scoped caching only if publication/auth rules remain correct.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Dynamic invalid IDs:

- legacy old path redirect occurs only for structurally valid paths.

Test malformed, unknown, archived, foreign IDs.

`/app/error.tsx` or equivalent:

- still offers Back to module.

Do not redirect every exception silently.

352. CANONICAL DASHBOARD RULE
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`/app` itself MUST be the canonical authenticated dashboard.

Do NOT make the ordinary final destination `/app/dashboard` unless repository truth proves an unavoidable constraint.

Target:

OLD:
  /dashboard

NEW:
  /app

Benefits:
- the application root is meaningful;
- login success has one obvious destination;
- bookmarks are shorter;
- installed/standalone web-app start URL can be `/app`;
- the shell's root state is unambiguous.

Compatibility:
`/dashboard` → permanent/internal compatibility redirect to `/app`.

If `/app/dashboard` temporarily exists during migration:
- it MUST not become a second canonical dashboard;
- redirect it to `/app` after migration;
- tests must assert only one final dashboard canonical URL.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
354. ROUTE INVENTORY AUTOMATION — DO NOT TRUST A HAND LIST
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Write or reuse a route inventory script that scans:

src/app/**/page.tsx
src/app/**/route.ts

The script must normalize route groups away and report:

- source file
- effective URL
- public/private
- role guard
- target `/app` URL
- shell/focus/public/API classification
- legacy redirect requirement
- canonical route status
- dynamic parameters

Run it before and after migration.

Acceptance:

BEFORE:
all existing routes inventoried.

AFTER:
all target routes inventoried;
no duplicate canonical private routes;
legacy aliases intentionally redirected;
APIs unchanged unless explicitly required by another accepted subsystem.

Fail if a new private page accidentally remains at a top-level namespace.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
355. LINK INVENTORY — EVERY INTERNAL HREF MUST BE MIGRATED
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Search the entire repository for internal destinations in:

Link href
router.push
router.replace
redirect()
permanentRedirect()
window.location
form action
safe next/default destinations
breadcrumbs
navigation registry
search-result hrefs
notification hrefs
audit/admin deep links
assignment links
email/reset links if they point to private destinations
test expectations
fixture route strings
documentation commands where operationally relevant.

Do NOT use a blind string replacement.

For each route:
- determine whether it is public, shell, focus, management or API;
- replace through canonical route helpers where appropriate;
- preserve dynamic IDs;
- preserve encoded query values;
- never prefix external URLs;
- never prefix `/api`.

Add a static guard/test that catches new source code using forbidden legacy private prefixes except inside:
- the legacy redirect compatibility map;
- migration documentation;
- explicit tests that verify redirects.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
356. ROUTE BUILDER — ONE SOURCE OF TRUTH
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Create or consolidate a typed route helper layer.

Conceptual examples:

routes.app.home()
routes.app.listening()
routes.app.listeningTest(id)
routes.app.readingAttempt(id)
routes.app.writingExam(id)
routes.app.speakingAi()
routes.app.mock(id)
routes.app.teacher.students()
routes.app.admin.content()
routes.app.owner.audit()

Requirements:
- URL construction is deterministic;
- IDs are encoded safely;
- query creation uses URLSearchParams or equivalent;
- route helpers do not know authorization secrets;
- UI and server code may share public route definitions where safe;
- APIs use a separate API route namespace/helper if useful;
- no circular mega-dependency.

CHILD-SIMPLE VERSION:
Do not make 200 people remember the address. Give everyone one address book.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
357. LEGACY PRIVATE URL REDIRECT ENGINE
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Implement explicit compatibility for old private URLs.

Required properties:
- same-origin only;
- preserve legitimate query parameters;
- dynamic route IDs preserved;
- no open redirect;
- no redirect loops;
- one hop wherever practical;
- old focus route goes to new focus route, not library root;
- old management route goes to corresponding `/app/...` management route;
- unknown malformed IDs keep normal 404 behavior;
- old POST/API URLs are NOT redirected as page aliases;
- canonical target returned before rendering obsolete page content.

Choose 307/308/Next redirect semantics deliberately.

Do not use client-side `useEffect(router.replace(...))` as the primary legacy redirect if a server redirect can answer immediately.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
358. SAFE `next=` MIGRATION
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Audit every login and auth continuation parameter.

Target examples:

/login?next=/app/reading
/login?next=/app/listening/tests/<id>

Requirements:
- only same-origin relative paths;
- private target normalized through canonical route policy;
- reject protocol-relative `//evil.example`;
- reject absolute external URL;
- reject encoded bypasses;
- preserve safe query;
- after successful auth, account status still decides whether target is allowed;
- pending/rejected/suspended cannot use `next` to bypass gates;
- management target rechecks current role from DB.

Tests must include malicious and legitimate values.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
359. ROOT ENTRY + INTRO VIDEO CONTRACT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Preserve the approved root experience.

`/` is not the authenticated application shell.

Required behavior:

ANONYMOUS:
/
→ approved intro/welcome behavior
→ login

ACTIVE AUTHENTICATED:
/
→ approved desktop intro where current product intentionally shows it
→ `/app`

PENDING/RESTRICTED:
/
→ approved intro/welcome behavior
→ `/pending`

Direct `/app` navigation:
- MUST NOT replay the marketing/entry video;
- MUST not show public welcome;
- goes directly through authenticated app gate.

Direct deep link `/app/reading/...`:
- MUST not bounce through `/`;
- auth gate handles it directly.

Keep current device-capability rule for the desktop intro unless measured evidence requires a deliberate change.
Do not replace it with user-agent sniffing.
Keep timeout/error/autoplay fallback.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

│   │   ├── layout.tsx                 # sidebar + topbar + main scroll + utilities
│   │   ├── page.tsx                   # /app dashboard
