----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
361. APP-LEVEL AUTHORIZATION LAYOUT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The `/app` parent layout may provide the broad active-account gate.

It MUST NOT replace page/API-specific authorization.

Broad gate:
- valid current session;
- user exists;
- current DB account status;
- redirect unauthenticated to login;
- redirect non-active status to correct account state.

Nested authorization:
- teacher pages: staff;
- admin pages: admin/owner;
- owner pages: owner;
- resource rows: row/scope checks;
- content drafts: publication/role checks;
- RIWI targets: capability/scope checks.

Never trust stale JWT role as final authorization.
Current DB truth remains authoritative.

Do not make every child call redundant expensive DB lookups if the architecture can safely cache the request-scoped current actor, but do not cache authorization across requests.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
362. SHELL LAYOUT PRESERVATION
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The existing Learners Area shell already solved important defects.

Preserve:

- `h-dvh`;
- document-level overflow locked for app shell;
- desktop rail independent scrolling;
- main content independent scrolling;
- `min-h-0` flex shrink behavior;
- sidebar hidden below mobile breakpoint;
- mobile drawer below the same breakpoint;
- safe-area padding;
- topbar always reachable;
- normal page content max width;
- Day/Night;
- UZ/EN;
- profile;
- notifications;
- global search;
- management mode;
- utility launcher.

`/app` migration is NOT permission to rewrite the shell from scratch.

Re-measure the shell after moving routes.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
363. BOOSTER-LIKE APP COHERENCE WITHOUT BOOSTER-LIKE CLIENT AUTH
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The desired similarity is PRODUCT COHERENCE, not implementation copying.

Safe principle:

ONE AUTHENTICATED APP
+ PERSISTENT NAV
+ CLEAR MODULE GROUPS
+ FAST TRANSITIONS
+ RESUMABLE LEARNING
+ PROGRESS
+ MOCKS
+ MANAGEMENT

Reject:

localStorage bearer token authority
client-only role gate
single giant HTML page
manual global DOM hide/show router
inline onclick handlers
hardcoded fake score
hardcoded course progress
proprietary Booster wording/content.

Learners Area remains:
Next App Router + server authorization + PostgreSQL + native components.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
364. APP NAVIGATION GROUPS
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Build navigation from canonical route definitions and role capabilities.

Recommended learner information architecture:

HOME
- Dashboard
- Live Classes
- Assignments

IELTS / LEARNING
- Listening
- Reading
- Writing
- Speaking
- Grammar
- Vocabulary
- TED / Video / Podcast as current product names justify

TRACK
- Mock Tests
- My Progress
- RIWI/Coach where product placement is appropriate

HELP / ACCOUNT
- Notifications where appropriate
- Support
- Profile

STAFF
- Management entry only when role permits

Do not make the nav so long that 20 items are equally prominent.
Use groups, hierarchy, and current content availability.

Do not hide a server-authorized route solely because one nav item is absent.
Nav visibility and route authorization remain separate.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
365. ACTIVE NAV MATCHING UNDER `/app`
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Audit every active-state rule.

Examples:

`/app/listening`
active Listening.

`/app/listening/tests/<id>`
Listening remains the semantic module even if normal shell is hidden.

`/app/admin/listening`
Management/Admin must be active, not learner Listening.

`/app/owner/dictionary`
Management/Owner active.

Use route metadata/prefix priority rather than brittle substring checks.

Tests:
- exact route;
- nested route;
- focus route;
- management route with same module word;
- query changes;
- unknown route.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
366. BREADCRUMBS UNDER `/app`
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Rebuild breadcrumb route entries around canonical `/app` paths.

Do not display a useless leading crumb literally named `app`.

Good:

Reading
› Passage
› Attempt

Management
› Listening
› Test

Owner
› Integrations

Not:

App
› App
› Reading
› Reading

Back target is a meaningful parent, not naive string truncation.

Breadcrumb links must all be canonical URLs.

Hard reload on any nested route must render the same breadcrumb hierarchy as client navigation.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
367. GLOBAL SEARCH UNDER `/app`
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Keep `/api/search` as API.

Returned internal hrefs must use canonical `/app` destinations.

Search may find:
- Reading content;
- Listening tests;
- Vocabulary;
- classes;
- other existing safe categories.

Server must continue role/publication filtering.

No result may point to:
- old top-level private URL;
- unauthorized draft;
- foreign learner resource;
- raw object URL.

Keyboard shortcut behavior remains correct.

Search query itself must not appear in fixed telemetry keys or logs containing private user text.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
368. NOTIFICATION LINK MIGRATION
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Audit stored/generated notification hrefs.

New notifications:
always store/generate canonical `/app` destinations.

Existing old stored hrefs:
must remain usable.

Options:
- normalize on read through the legacy route map;
- or safely migrate stored internal hrefs with an audited DB migration.

Do not rewrite external links.

Do not accidentally double-prefix `/app/app`.

A notification referencing content that no longer exists must render a truthful unavailable state, not crash the shell.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
369. ASSIGNMENT LINK MIGRATION
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Assignments may reference canonical content.

After Content OS Phase 2, prefer content/version identity over storing fragile URL strings.

If assignment row currently stores href:
- migrate/normalize safely;
- preserve historical assignment;
- use canonical route resolver.

New assignment routes live under `/app/assignments`.

A student must never use a crafted assignment link to access:
- another student's work;
- unpublished content;
- staff-only editor;
- a newer content version than assigned when version binding matters.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
370. APP MANIFEST — INSTALLABLE WEB APP METADATA
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Add a Learners Area web app manifest if not already present and if implementation is compatible with current deployment.

Target concepts:

name: Learners Area
short_name: Learners Area
start_url: /app
scope: /
display: standalone
background/theme colors: Learners Area token-derived compatible colors
icons: approved Learners Area derivatives

Do not copy Booster manifest values/assets.

Do not claim:
offline capability
native app capability
push capability
background sync

merely because a manifest exists.

Manifest installation is optional enhancement.
The core `/app` architecture must work perfectly in an ordinary browser.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
371. SERVICE WORKER — DEFAULT NO
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Do NOT add a service worker just because the product uses `/app`.

A stale service worker can break:
- authentication;
- private response caching;
- deployments;
- asset versions;
- security headers.

Only add one if there is a separately defined, tested offline/cache requirement.

If no such requirement exists:
manifest may exist;
service worker does not.

Document this deliberate decision.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
372. NO PRIVATE HTML IN SEARCH ENGINE INDEX
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
All `/app/**` pages are private and must retain noindex/nofollow/nocache intent.

Root/public marketing pages may be indexable according to current deployment/environment policy.

Sitemap:
- do not list private `/app/**`;
- do not list `/api/**`;
- do not list account-internal routes.

robots:
preserve Preview noindex behavior.

Do not leak route IDs or user-specific URLs into SEO metadata.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
373. APP METADATA / DOCUMENT TITLE
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Set useful page titles without leaking private content.

Examples:
Learners Area — Dashboard
Learners Area — Listening
Learners Area — Reading
Learners Area — Management

Dynamic learner submissions should not put private answer text in browser title.

Do not expose:
student email
internal DB ID
provider/model
storage key
report body

in metadata.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
374. HARD RELOAD IS A FIRST-CLASS TEST
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Every canonical `/app` page must work on direct hard reload.

Do NOT accept a route that works only after navigating there from Dashboard.

Test:
paste deep URL in address bar;
reload;
open in a new tab;
navigate Back/Forward.

Especially:
dynamic attempts
mock runner
Writing exam
Listening focus
Reading focus
admin editors
owner pages.

Next server routing, auth and data loading must reconstruct the state.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
375. BROWSER HISTORY CONTRACT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Do not replace Next/browser history with a custom page stack.

Expected behavior:

Link navigation
→ URL changes

Back
→ prior meaningful screen

Forward
→ restored next screen

Filters encoded in URL
→ restored on Back

Focus attempt
→ Back returns library when appropriate

No double entries caused by:
client redirect after server redirect;
both onClick router.push and Link default;
temporary alias chain.

Test browser history length and user-visible destination, not just href strings.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
376. SCROLL RESTORATION CONTRACT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Important flows:

library scroll
→ open item
→ Back
→ return near prior library position where Next/browser semantics support it.

Do not force `window.scrollTo(0,0)` globally.

Focus routes may intentionally start at top.

Management lists should preserve:
filters
page
search
where practical.

No custom scroll restoration may leak across users.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
377. SHELL STATE VS SERVER LEARNING STATE
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
UI-only state may live locally:
- drawer open;
- utility panel open;
- focus preference;
- temporary tab presentation where URL state is not required.

Learning truth must remain server-authoritative:
- answers;
- scores;
- attempt status;
- course completion;
- mastery;
- streak;
- assignment state;
- mock result.

Do not adopt Booster localStorage score/mastery patterns.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
378. APP-WIDE ERROR BOUNDARY CONTRACT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The `/app` hierarchy needs scoped failures.

One failing secondary region must not blank the entire application when isolation is possible.

Provide:
- app-level fatal error boundary;
- route-level error boundaries where useful;
- region failure notices for independent data;
- retry;
- correlation IDs where safe;
- no raw server error text.

A private server exception must not reveal:
SQL
stack trace
environment variable
storage host secrets
provider request payload.

Do not turn every exception into "Something went wrong" if a specific safe action can be shown.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
379. APP-WIDE LOADING CONTRACT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Do not reintroduce the historical blanket 300ms fallback delay.

Use:
- immediate pressed/pending state on the control;
- preserve previous page while Next route data arrives when beneficial;
- local skeleton only for truly streamed/slow regions;
- meaningful fallback for genuinely slow route boundaries.

No full-screen spinner for every click.

No fake progress.

No permanent shimmer after error.

Measure the result.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
380. APP-WIDE EMPTY STATE CONTRACT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Every major collection needs a truthful empty state.

Examples:
No assignments.
No mock history.
No vocabulary due.
No lessons published.
No notifications.
No student rows in permitted scope.

An empty state must not look like:
broken page;
loading forever;
blank white rectangle.

If content is unavailable due to missing schema/deployment:
show unavailable, not empty.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
381. APP-WIDE BUTTON CONTRACT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
All ordinary actions must use Learners Area primitives/tokens.

Required:
- rounded geometry;
- consistent min touch target;
- visible focus;
- disabled semantics;
- pending state;
- no unexplained browser-default square button;
- destructive action differentiated but accessible;
- no color-only meaning.

Do not make module-specific global CSS overwrite shared buttons accidentally.

This specifically guards against the prior Listening purple/square-button regression.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
382. APP-WIDE FORM CONTRACT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Forms must:
- label every input;
- preserve typed values on recoverable error where safe;
- prevent accidental duplicate submit;
- show field/server errors;
- release pending state;
- support keyboard;
- fit mobile keyboard viewport;
- not send secrets to client logs.

Mutation success must be confirmed by server response.
Do not optimistically show irreversible success before authority confirms.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
383. APP-WIDE MODAL / DIALOG CONTRACT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Dialogs:
- real accessible dialog semantics;
- focus enters;
- focus cannot vanish behind overlay;
- Escape behavior when safe;
- close control;
- focus returns;
- mobile viewport fit;
- body scroll lock cleanup;
- no nested z-index chaos.

Destructive confirmation dialog must name what will happen.

Do not use `window.confirm()` if existing native design dialog infrastructure is available and tested.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
384. URL QUERY CONTRACT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Use query parameters for shareable/filter state where appropriate:

/app/reading?tab=...
/app/listening?page=...
/app/admin/writing?section=...

Requirements:
- typed/sanitized;
- bounded numbers;
- unknown values fall to safe default;
- query survives canonical legacy redirect;
- route helpers serialize consistently;
- no secret/private free text in URL unless intentionally safe.

Do not store user answers in URL.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
385. DYNAMIC PARAMETER CONTRACT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
All dynamic IDs from URL:
- validate format early;
- enforce ownership/publication;
- 404 missing/malformed where appropriate;
- do not distinguish foreign object from missing if doing so leaks existence;
- no SQL interpolation;
- no raw storage path traversal.

Moving under `/app` must not weaken existing `isUuid` or equivalent checks.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
386. MANAGEMENT MODE INSIDE `/app`
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Keep staff management as a mode of the same authenticated product.

Target:

/app/management
/app/teacher/...
/app/admin/...
/app/owner/...

Shell may show management navigation instead of learner navigation.

Always provide:
← Back to learning

Returning goes to `/app` or meaningful prior learning destination.

A bookmark to `/app/admin/content` must enter management mode directly.

Do not require user to click a hidden mode toggle first.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
387. ROLE-AWARE SHELL WITHOUT ROLE-AUTHORIZATION CONFUSION
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Sidebar/nav may render different items per role.

But server pages/APIs enforce real authority.

Test:
student manually enters /app/admin/content → refused/redirected appropriately.
teacher manually enters /app/owner → refused.
admin attempts owner-only mutation → refused.
suspended user with old cookie → refused.

Do not rely on `role` copied from client JS.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
388. PROFILE AND ACCOUNT SURFACE
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reconcile current product truth before creating new UI.

If `/profile` already exists:
move to `/app/profile`.

If current tested product intentionally uses ProfileMenu as the only profile surface:
do not invent an empty `/app/profile` just to fill a nav row.

Any edit capability must be real and server-authorized.

Keep:
sign out
current identity
role-safe display
locale/theme integrations

truthful.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
389. COURSE SWITCHING — DO NOT INVENT A FAKE SWITCHER
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Current product historically had one course and deliberately removed a fake IELTS switcher.

If Master Prompt 2 introduces a real course registry:
add course-aware navigation only when at least two meaningful eligible courses exist or product explicitly wants a selector.

If only IELTS exists:
do not render a fake dropdown with one item.

Architecture may be future-ready without pretending SAT exists.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
390. FUTURE SAT URL STRATEGY
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Do not bake all app URLs into a structure that makes future courses impossible.

However, do not prematurely change every current IELTS route to `/app/courses/ielts/...` if that harms usability.

Acceptable strategy:
- primary IELTS modules remain concise `/app/reading`, `/app/listening`, etc.;
- shared content entities carry course identity;
- future SAT gets `/app/sat/...` or selected course context through a deliberate future ADR.

What matters:
shared shell, content OS, publication, assets, assignments, roles and history are course-capable.

Do not invent unapproved SAT UI now.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
391. FOCUS LAYOUT — APP-LEVEL AUTH WITHOUT SHELL CHROME
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The new `/app` hierarchy must allow focus pages to share the active-user gate without sharing the ordinary sidebar/topbar.

This is why the recommended tree separates:

app/layout.tsx
    active-user gate

app/(shell)/layout.tsx
    ordinary shell

app/(focus)/layout.tsx
    full-focus shell

Focus layout includes only what the assessment needs:
- safe Back;
- test/workspace;
- required timer/status;
- required accessibility;
- perhaps report support if product decides and it does not obstruct exam.

Do not render hidden sidebar markup and merely set `display:none` if clean route-group layout can avoid it.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
392. FOCUS BACK CONTROL
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Every focus surface needs an escape route.

Use current BackLink/navigation semantics.

Requirements:
- top-left;
- visible;
- Learners Area button geometry;
- history-aware;
- safe canonical fallback;
- not covered by mobile safe area;
- keyboard focusable;
- no browser-default appearance.

Fallback examples:
Listening → /app/listening
Reading → /app/reading
Writing → /app/writing
Mock → /app/mocks

Do not allow a formal attempt to lose required autosave merely because Back is clicked.
Handle leave policy truthfully.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
393. MOCK RUNNER UNDER `/app`
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Master Prompt 2 owns mock domain architecture.

This prompt owns canonical app routing and UX integration.

Target:
`/app/mocks` = catalogue/history entry.

Formal run:
`/app/mocks/<mockId>/...`
under focus layout.

Requirements:
- exact content-version composition;
- server timing;
- refresh resume;
- no ordinary app sidebar;
- canonical exit behavior;
- section transitions;
- result route under `/app/mocks/...` or canonical history destination;
- legacy routes redirect if earlier work created different paths.

Do not combine a full mock into an unbounded client page.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
394. DASHBOARD AS APPLICATION CONTROL CENTER
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`/app` dashboard should answer:

What should I continue?
What is assigned?
What is open now?
How am I progressing?
What needs review?

Use real server data.

Potential cards:
- Continue where you left off;
- assignments;
- live class status;
- retention/review due;
- recent result;
- mock progress;
- course roadmap.

Do not show a card just because Booster has one.
Only show a concept when Learners Area has truthful backing data.

No fake "Day 17", fake XP, fake streak or fake percentage.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
395. DASHBOARD QUERY BUDGET
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Audit `/app` dashboard for waterfall/N+1 behavior.

Independent reads should run concurrently where safe.

Use bounded summary queries.

Do not fetch:
full passage body
40 question rows
full transcripts
audio URLs
entire evaluation history

to draw summary cards.

Add query-count/performance evidence if diagnostics exist.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
396. APP-WIDE SERVER COMPONENT BIAS
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Keep static/data presentation on server components where appropriate.

Use client components for:
- interactive controls;
- recording;
- browser speech APIs;
- local form state;
- dialogs;
- optimistic pending;
- browser-only media features.

Do not add `"use client"` to `/app/layout.tsx` and drag the entire private app into one client bundle.

Preserve Next server rendering, auth and streaming strengths.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
397. CLIENT BUNDLE HYGIENE
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Measure route bundles after migration.

Watch for accidentally global imports:
- PDF parser;
- fflate/ZIP logic;
- AWS SDK;
- RIWI provider code;
- huge admin forms;
- test renderer;
- media recorder;
- full question registries.

Server-only dependencies must remain server-only.

Dynamic import heavy client-only authoring tools only where used.

No module should make Dashboard download its importer.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
398. SERVER-ONLY BOUNDARY
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Secrets and privileged services remain server-only.

Never client-bundle:
database URL
R2 secret
provider API key
AUTH_SECRET
owner policy internals that are not learner-safe
server evaluator prompt internals
backup credentials.

Use `server-only` guard where repository conventions support it.

Build/static tests should catch accidental exposure.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
399. RSC PAYLOAD PRIVACY
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A Server Component can still serialize props to a Client Component.

Audit client-bound props.

Do not pass:
password hash
provider credentials
raw DB user row
private audit metadata
answer key during active assessment
foreign user IDs unnecessarily
signed URLs farther than needed
RIWI provider/model internals

merely because data was fetched server-side.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
400. API NAMESPACE STABILITY
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Keep current `/api/*` namespace unless a specific accepted subsystem requires a new endpoint.

Do not rename 100 APIs solely to mirror `/app`.

Page migration and API migration are different problems.

Changing both at once increases regression risk.

Existing APIs may gain canonical content/version contracts from Master Prompts 1/2, but `/app` conversion itself should not churn stable HTTP interfaces without cause.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
401. API CALLERS AFTER PAGE ROUTE MIGRATION
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Even though APIs stay `/api`, audit API callers for page-route assumptions.

Examples:
- response `href` fields;
- success redirect destinations;
- notification creation;
- audit deep links;
- assignment destination;
- export links;
- support report current path;
- callback continuation;
- generated emails/messages.

Never prefix API URL with `/app`.

Never leave response page destination at old `/reading` when canonical is `/app/reading`.

Build a source-level test for known internal href producers.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
402. SUPPORT REPORT ROUTE CONTEXT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Support reports may record where a problem occurred.

After migration:
new reports should record canonical `/app/...` route context.

Historical reports with old route path remain truthful historical data.
Do not rewrite the original incident path merely for cosmetic consistency.

When rendering a historical route as a clickable reproduction link:
normalize through compatibility mapping if safe.

Never allow stored report path to become an open redirect.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
403. AUDIT LOG ROUTE CONTEXT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Audit events record action truth, not UI architecture.

Do not mass-rewrite historical audit metadata.

New route-related audit metadata should use canonical route class or stable target identity, not fragile full URLs where possible.

No sensitive query parameters in audit logs.

Keep target IDs/actions stable through route migration.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
404. CONTENT OS ADMIN INTEGRATION
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Master Prompt 1/2 may introduce new content-authoring surfaces.

All those surfaces belong under:

/app/admin/...
or
/app/teacher/...
or
/app/owner/...

according to role.

The app conversion must inventory newly created pages AFTER Master Prompt 2, not rely on this historical route list.

Every new content OS screen must receive:
- canonical route;
- breadcrumb;
- management nav;
- authorization;
- responsive behavior;
- error/loading state;
- deep-link reload;
- browser QA.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
405. RIWI FINAL INTEGRATION — DO NOT LOSE PARALLEL SECURITY WORK
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
RIWI currently lives on a parallel accepted/security workstream.

Before final `/app` implementation closure:
- fetch latest RIWI authoritative branch;
- compare with current implementation branch;
- identify source/test/docs changes not yet integrated;
- identify migration-number collisions;
- identify overlapping Coach/Speaking/auth/rate-limit/schema files;
- integrate deliberately on a dedicated final integration branch or the authorized task branch;
- do not merge blindly;
- rerun RIWI full security/assessment gates after conflict resolution.

Routing changes required for RIWI:
- `/coach` → `/app/coach`;
- any owner RIWI control routes → `/app/owner/...`;
- notification/report links canonicalized;
- APIs remain `/api/...`.

Do not alter RIWI hard-core contract or provider governance merely because routes move.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
406. MIGRATION NUMBER COLLISION FORENSICS
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Parallel workstreams may independently add Drizzle migrations with overlapping numbers.

Before integration:
- list journal entries;
- list migration files;
- compare parent snapshots;
- compare database semantic changes;
- do not resolve collision by filename rename alone unless snapshot/journal semantics remain valid;
- regenerate/reconcile according to Drizzle workflow;
- test fresh migration;
- test populated upgrade.

Never drop one migration because another branch used the same number.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
407. DICTIONARY REPOSITORY BOUNDARY
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The separate dictionary project/repository must not be confused with Learners Area route migration.

Do not execute commands in:
`~/Desktop/project`
or any dictionary repository
when this task targets `N-Muhammadjonov/learners_area`.

Learners Area's in-app Dictionary/lexical interfaces remain under canonical `/app` owner/learner surfaces as designed.

External dictionary data/release ingestion follows its own accepted workflow.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
408. PUBLIC LINK / TELEGRAM / EXTERNAL URL CONTRACT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Do not prefix external links with `/app`.

Examples:
Telegram
YouTube
external lesson source
external video provider
documentation/support URL

Use normal external-link security:
- correct target behavior;
- rel attributes where needed;
- no opener leakage where applicable.

Internal Telegram login callback URL is auth infrastructure; migrate only its final safe destination.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
409. DEEP LINK FROM TELEGRAM / EMAIL
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
If product sends internal deep links:
new links should use canonical `/app/...`.

Old links must continue through compatibility redirects during supported migration window.

Authentication:
deep link while logged out
→ login
→ safe next
→ original canonical target after server authorization.

No role bypass.
No content publication bypass.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
410. AUTH PROVIDER CALLBACKS
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Audit:
Google callback
Telegram callback
password reset completion
registration/onboarding continuation.

Do not change provider callback endpoint URLs from `/api/auth/...` merely because app pages move.

Only change post-auth destinations:
active → `/app` or safe `/app/...` next
pending → `/pending`
onboarding required → `/onboarding`

Verify configured redirect origins/domains separately from route path migration.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
411. COOKIE PATH / SAME-SITE AUDIT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Ensure session/theme/locale cookies remain available where intended after `/app` migration.

Do not accidentally set session cookie Path to an obsolete top-level route.

Session cookie:
secure
HttpOnly where appropriate
SameSite according to auth flow
path broad enough for `/app` and APIs.

Theme/locale cookies may be readable according to current server implementation.

Do not widen cookie scope to unrelated domains.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
412. CSP / SECURITY HEADERS AFTER `/app`
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Current middleware applies CSP/security headers globally.

Retest:
public root
auth pages
/app
/app focus pages
/api
resource redirects/streams
legacy redirects
404

Listening legacy sandbox, if still present after Content OS migration, must retain its intentionally isolated CSP only for the exact sandbox API route.

Do not make CSP globally permissive to fix one legacy renderer.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
413. ORIGIN CHECK AFTER `/app`
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
State-changing APIs remain protected by request-origin verification.

Moving UI pages must not alter:
- allowed same-origin semantics;
- CSRF posture;
- API mutation origin checks.

Preview branch aliases and Production domain must be handled by current host-aware policy.

Do not whitelist arbitrary Vercel domains with `*` for convenience without understanding the risk.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
414. R2 CORS VS APP URL PATH
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
R2 CORS cares about ORIGIN, not path.

Changing:
`/listening` → `/app/listening`

does not require a new R2 CORS origin if scheme+host+port are unchanged.

Do not add `/app` path to `AllowedOrigins`.

Keep stable Preview/Production origin policy from the storage workstream.

This simple fact must be documented to avoid future configuration mistakes.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
415. PUBLIC BASE URL / CANONICAL URL
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Audit `publicBaseUrl`.

Root public metadata may continue to canonicalize `/`.

Private `/app` pages should not advertise public canonical URLs containing user-specific paths.

If installed-app metadata uses `start_url`, use `/app`.

Do not make Preview URL a permanent production canonical URL.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
416. DEPLOYMENT ALIAS CONTRACT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
For Preview acceptance prefer a stable branch alias when available.

Why:
- R2 CORS origin can be stable;
- OAuth callback testing is reproducible;
- owner bookmarks remain usable;
- QA does not chase random deployment IDs.

Still record exact deployment SHA/URL for evidence.

Do not confuse stable alias with proof that the latest build succeeded.
Verify deployment commit.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
417. VERSION ENDPOINT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Preserve or improve `/api/version`.

It should provide safe deployment/build identity needed for QA:
- commit if platform provides it;
- environment;
- region if already safe;
- no secret.

Acceptance evidence should match:
local HEAD
remote HEAD
deployed version.

If platform does not expose commit:
report UNVERIFIED rather than fabricate.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
418. PREVIEW BEFORE PRODUCTION
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Final `/app` conversion must be accepted on Preview before Production.

Preview acceptance includes:
- migrations;
- auth;
- role navigation;
- module routes;
- focus routes;
- content;
- R2;
- RIWI where authorized;
- mobile/desktop;
- redirects;
- deep reload;
- performance.

Production migration/deployment requires separate explicit authorization and recovery evidence.

Do not automatically deploy Production.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
419. ROLLBACK PLAN
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Before Production approval prepare:

CODE ROLLBACK:
known previous good SHA.

DB ROLLBACK:
provider safety point / forward-fix plan appropriate to additive migrations.

ROUTE ROLLBACK:
legacy redirects remain capable of reaching the old equivalent only if code rollback occurs.

ASSET ROLLBACK:
no destructive move without retained source window.

Do not rely on fake SQL down migration for unsafe schema changes.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
420. LEGACY ROUTE SUPPORT WINDOW
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Do not remove compatibility redirects immediately after the first successful Preview.

Define a support horizon based on:
- saved bookmarks;
- notifications;
- emails;
- historical audit/support links;
- external shared links.

Instrument aggregate legacy-route use only if privacy-safe and existing observability supports it.

Never log full sensitive query payload just to count redirects.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
421. 404 / NOT FOUND CONTRACT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Canonical `/app` 404 behavior:
- malformed dynamic ID → 404;
- missing content → 404 or safe unavailable according to existing product;
- foreign private object should not leak existence;
- legacy known route → redirect;
- unknown old route → normal 404.

Do not redirect every unknown `/app/*` to Dashboard.
That hides broken links and makes QA impossible.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
422. PUBLIC 404 VS APP 404
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Public 404 may use public presentation.

Authenticated app 404 should offer a safe way back to `/app` without leaking shell state if the failure occurred in focus mode.

Do not render admin nav on a student 404.

Do not turn a permission failure into a misleading generic 404 where current security policy intentionally uses redirect/403.
Follow repository conventions.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
423. MOBILE INSTALLED / STANDALONE MODE
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
If manifest install is enabled, test standalone display.

Check:
- safe areas;
- topbar;
- mobile drawer;
- virtual keyboard;
- Back behavior;
- external links;
- file picker;
- microphone;
- audio;
- full-focus;
- login redirect;
- sign out.

Do not rely on browser chrome Back button being present in standalone mode.
Therefore every nested/focus experience needs in-app navigation.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
424. IOS SAFARI / ANDROID CHROME REALITY
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Web-app behavior differs across mobile browsers.

Do not claim installability parity or media API parity without testing.

Key checks:
- `100dvh`;
- safe-area insets;
- file picker;
- MediaRecorder;
- SpeechRecognition support differences;
- audio autoplay rules;
- keyboard resize;
- standalone navigation.

Feature-detect.
Render truthful fallback.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
425. DESKTOP BROWSER MATRIX
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
At minimum test current supported desktop targets available to the project:

Chromium-family
and Safari/WebKit where tooling/device permits.

Firefox if product support policy includes it.

Do not say cross-browser PASS from Chromium alone.

Classify unsupported browser-dependent features separately from general app routing.

- skip to main;

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
433. LEGACY REDIRECT ACCEPTANCE MATRIX
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
For every legacy private page mapping in Section 353, create an automated redirect case.

Each case must assert:
- old URL answers with intended redirect semantics;
- target begins with canonical `/app` private namespace;
- dynamic ID preserved exactly;
- safe query preserved;
- fragment behavior follows browser semantics where applicable;
- no redirect loop;
- target requires correct auth;
- one-hop target where practical;
- final rendered canonical URL contains no old private prefix.

Additionally test:
`/dashboard` → `/app`.
`/app/dashboard` → `/app` if temporary alias exists.
unknown old URL → 404, not Dashboard.
malformed dynamic ID → 404 after/without safe mapping according to route contract.
external URL-like `next` → refused.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
434. CRITICAL END-TO-END USER JOURNEYS
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The final browser suite must execute real journeys, not isolated page opens.

JOURNEY 1 — NEW ACTIVE STUDENT
login
→ /app
→ open Reading
→ start attempt
→ answer
→ autosave
→ submit
→ review
→ Back/history
→ progress reflects real work

JOURNEY 2 — LISTENING
/app/listening
→ open test
→ full focus
→ audio
→ answers
→ save
→ submit/review
→ Back
→ library state preserved

JOURNEY 3 — WRITING
/app/writing
→ select task
→ formal workspace
→ draft persists
→ submit
→ evaluation path
→ history

JOURNEY 4 — SPEAKING AI
/app/speaking/ai
→ microphone gate
→ mode
→ server plan
→ record
→ STOP does not send
→ review transcript
→ Send to RIWI
→ feedback
→ next
→ summary/history

JOURNEY 5 — VOCABULARY
lookup
→ canonical sense
→ save
→ review due
→ grade/review
→ progress

JOURNEY 6 — FULL MOCK
/app/mocks
→ start exact version
→ formal focus runner
→ refresh mid-run
→ server state resumes
→ complete
→ results/history

JOURNEY 7 — TEACHER
/app/management
→ students
→ scoped student
→ assign canonical content
→ learner completes
→ teacher sees allowed result

JOURNEY 8 — ADMIN
/app/admin/content
→ import/create content
→ validate
→ preview
→ draft
→ publish
→ learner sees it

JOURNEY 9 — OWNER
/app/owner
→ audit/integrations/RIWI policy surfaces
→ permitted action
→ audit record
→ no secret exposed

JOURNEY 10 — LEGACY BOOKMARK
old private URL
→ login if needed
→ canonical /app destination
→ same intended content.

Each journey must define:
actor
seed data
starting URL
steps
expected persistent state
expected final URL
network errors
console errors
cleanup.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
435. OFFLINE / NETWORK INTERRUPTION TRUTH
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The product is online-first unless a separate offline feature is intentionally implemented.

Test failure behavior:

route RSC fetch offline
API mutation offline
audio resource unavailable
R2 timeout
RIWI provider timeout
database unavailable
network recovers

Required:
- no fake success;
- no permanent pending;
- typed work preserved where safe;
- retry available where meaningful;
- submitted state not duplicated after uncertain response;
- no claim of offline mode.

Do not add cache magic to hide server failure.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
436. MULTI-TAB CONSISTENCY
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Test two tabs for important mutable flows.

Examples:
same Reading attempt;
same Writing draft;
same mock;
same assignment;
profile/account status change.

Server rules win.

If one tab submits:
the other tab must not overwrite final state with stale autosave.

If account becomes suspended:
next protected request rejects even if another tab has old UI.

If publication changes:
new start obeys new policy while historical attempt remains readable where accepted.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
437. RACE / DOUBLE-CLICK MATRIX
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Test rapid duplicate actions:

login submit
start attempt
submit attempt
publish content
upload intent
finalize upload
Send to RIWI
assignment submit
mock complete
role/status change
notification acknowledge

Each must be:
idempotent
transactionally guarded
or explicitly reject duplicate in a safe deterministic way.

UI lock is helpful but server uniqueness/status guards are authoritative.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
438. APP PERFORMANCE BUDGETS
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Use measured budgets as goals, not fabricated guarantees.

Recommended product targets to investigate on representative Preview:
- local control acknowledgement: visually immediate, target under ~150ms;
- warm navigation meaningful content: target under ~1s;
- p95 representative remote app navigation: target around <=1.5s where infrastructure permits;
- no repeated unexplained 5–10 second freezes.

Historical local measurements are evidence of earlier architecture, not current final proof.

Measure:
click→pending feedback
click→meaningful content
RSC/API duration
TTFB
long tasks
bundle transfer
LCP where meaningful
INP if tooling supports it.

Document environment and sample size.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
439. PERFORMANCE REGRESSION GUARDS
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Specifically prevent reintroduction of known failures:

- blanket route fallback adding artificial ~300ms delay;
- N+1 query per question/card;
- desktop rail squeezing mobile main column;
- giant import code loaded on Dashboard;
- serialized independent DB reads;
- full content fetched for library cards;
- unnecessary revalidation loops;
- client page switcher that mounts all modules at once.

Use causal measurement before/after optimization.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
440. DATABASE CONNECTION / POOL BEHAVIOR
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Route migration may increase shared layout/data calls.

Audit managed PostgreSQL connection use:
- no new connection per component;
- reuse repository DB client/pool strategy;
- no leaked transactions;
- transactions short;
- no DB access from Edge middleware;
- request-level parallel reads reasonable;
- pooler compatibility documented.

Do not move DB authorization into middleware; current Edge limitation remains.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
441. OBSERVABILITY AFTER ROUTE MIGRATION
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Update safe observability categories.

Metrics/logs should prefer route/workspace keys:
dashboard
listening
reading
writing
speaking
grammar
vocabulary
mocks
management
etc.

Do not emit:
raw dynamic path IDs
search terms
student answer text
report body
transcript
email
token
signed URL.

Legacy redirect counts may use fixed route-class key.

Errors need correlation ID without sensitive payload.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
442. STATIC SOURCE SWEEP
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Before final acceptance search source for obsolete route literals.

Forbidden examples outside approved compatibility code/tests/docs:

href="/dashboard"
href="/reading"
router.push("/listening")
redirect("/management")
`/owner/...` learner-facing canonical link
`/admin/...` canonical page link

Do not blindly flag:
`/api/...`
public auth routes
external URL
documentation historical evidence
legacy redirect map itself.

Create a guarded allowlist, not an unreadable regex exception jungle.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
443. BUILT OUTPUT / SOURCE-MAP SWEEP
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Final production build:
- no browser source maps;
- no secret env values in client JS;
- no unexpected old route strings in navigation bundles beyond compatibility requirements;
- no giant unintended server-only SDK in client chunks;
- no framework default branding.

Preserve current source-map minimization and powered-by policy.

3. THE 12 NON-NEGOTIABLE RIWI LAWS
====================================================================================================
RIWI LAW #1 — SAFETY BOUNDARY
RIWI must never modify Learners Area source code, corrupt application behavior, modify Production infrastructure, expose secrets, or transmit protected Learners Area data externally except through an explicitly authorized, bounded, audited tool.
RIWI LAW #2 — DENY BY DEFAULT
Anything not explicitly allowed is denied.
RIWI LAW #3 — DATA MINIMIZATION
External providers receive only the minimum task-required content.
RIWI LAW #4 — AUTHORITATIVE DATA WINS
Database/dictionary/approved Learners Area sources outrank model memory for deterministic facts.
RIWI LAW #5 — NO BLIND SELF-TRAINING
Unverified model output never becomes active knowledge automatically.
RIWI LAW #6 — TRUTHFUL PROVENANCE
Internally preserve actual provider/model/version/fallback/source.
RIWI LAW #7 — NO RAW SECRETS
RIWI never receives DB passwords, provider secrets, R2 secrets, SSH keys or service credentials.
RIWI LAW #8 — TOOLS, NOT ARBITRARY EXECUTION
Owner power comes through approved server tools, not shell/SQL/filesystem/network freedom.
RIWI LAW #9 — ROLE AND ROW SCOPE
Teacher/student/admin scope must be enforced at data/tool layer.
RIWI LAW #10 — FAIL CLOSED
Broken policy/configuration never broadens access.
RIWI LAW #11 — AUDIT HIGH-IMPACT ACTIONS
High-impact actions and knowledge promotions are auditable.
RIWI LAW #12 — NO FAKE CERTAINTY
Insufficient evidence is reported as uncertainty rather than invented fact.

```text
      +------ NO ------> DENY
      |
      YES
      |
      v
BOUND SERVICE FUNCTION
      |
      v
SCHEMA-VALIDATED RESULT
      |
      v
AUDIT + RIWI RESPONSE
```

OWNER: "How many learners used Listening today?"
RIWI: Call deterministic reporting tool and explain result.
OWNER: "Show students whose Reading progress fell this month."
RIWI: Use deterministic scoped analytics.

RIWI: Retrieve real metrics; distinguish facts from inference.

RIWI: Ingest as candidate knowledge; owner review before active use.
OWNER: "Use this corrected essay as a gold example."
RIWI: Store versioned owner-verified example and regression evidence.
OWNER: "Disable this learner account."
RIWI: Use explicit owner tool, verify target, audit action.
OWNER: "Switch Writing evaluation to Claude model X."
RIWI: Validate provider/model and update owner policy; never reveal secret.
OWNER: "Compare DeepSeek, Qwen and Claude on this rubric."
RIWI: Run owner evaluation experiment with minimized payload.
OWNER: "Explain this dictionary phrase in Uzbek."
RIWI: Retrieve canonical sense first.
OWNER: "Export this month engagement report."
RIWI: Use Reporter export; AI not used for numeric path.

WHY: Owner needs broad control without infrastructure credentials.

TEST: Owner-only authorization + browser tests.
EVIDENCE: Owner UI evidence.

TEST: Ambiguous target, stale target, replay tests.
EVIDENCE: Audit receipt.

- Dictionary-grounded vocabulary.
- Own progress only.
- Own evaluation feedback.

- Review permitted submissions.
- Submit candidate corrections.
- No owner provider/secret/global audit access.

- No implicit owner power.
- No provider secret access.
- Reports only in explicit admin scope.

13. EXTERNAL DATA GUARD — PRIVACY BEFORE PROVIDER CALL
====================================================================================================
NEVER SEND BY DEFAULT:
- email
- Telegram id/username
- phone
- password
- session token
- account id
- raw DB id
- full account history
- unrelated learning history
- owner private notes
- provider keys
- R2 keys
- DATABASE_URL
- service-role key
- SSH credentials
- other students data
STRUCTURAL DIAGRAM

14. NETWORK / SSRF SECURITY
====================================================================================================
- HTTPS only
- reject localhost
- reject loopback IPv4/IPv6
- reject link-local
- reject metadata endpoints
- reject unauthorized private networks
- normalize hostname
- DNS validate before every call
- resist DNS rebinding
- redirect:error or revalidate redirects
- no URL credentials
- server-controlled provider endpoints
- sanitized external research only

28. MEMORY MODEL — DO NOT MIX EVERYTHING
====================================================================================================
SESSION MEMORY
  Short-lived conversation context; no cross-user bleed.
USER LEARNING MEMORY
  Learner-specific authorized progress/preferences.
KNOWLEDGE MEMORY
  Approved versioned educational/domain knowledge.
EVALUATION MEMORY
  Provider outputs/comparisons/corrections/outcomes.
POLICY MEMORY
  Owner-approved RIWI rules/configuration.
FAILURE MEMORY
  Sanitized failure patterns.
AUDIT MEMORY
  Governance/action history, not ordinary semantic knowledge.

29. RESPONSE TRUTHFULNESS
====================================================================================================
- Deterministic facts use authoritative internal data.
- Generated explanation is not presented as stored dictionary fact.
- Unknown remains unknown.
- Ambiguity is acknowledged.
- External failure is not hidden.
- Fallback is internally recorded.
- Learner can see Checked by RIWI while owner can see real provenance.
- No hidden chain-of-thought disclosure; concise evidence summary only.

====================================================================================================
- provider timeout
- rate limit
- malformed output
- provider unavailable
- knowledge unavailable
- dictionary unavailable
- report query failure
- permission denied
- target not found
- audit failure
- redaction failure
- owner config unreadable
- DB transient error
- stale knowledge version
- knowledge conflict
- no retrieval result
NO infinite spinner. NO permanently disabled button. NO fake success. NO raw vendor body. NO permission broadening.

35. CONCEPTUAL DATA MODEL — REUSE EXISTING TABLES FIRST
====================================================================================================
- riwi_knowledge_sources: source metadata/version/provenance/state/scope/supersedes
- riwi_knowledge_units: parsed units linked to source
- riwi_knowledge_conflicts: candidate vs active conflict/resolution
- riwi_learning_signals: raw/candidate evidence
- riwi_learning_reviews: trusted review decision
- riwi_policy_versions: versioned behavior/policy if needed
- existing audit extension: tool/action metadata
- riwi_provider_experiments: owner benchmark metadata
- riwi_provider_experiment_results: normalized provider outcomes
- riwi_usage_metrics: sanitized usage/latency/cost
- riwi_conversation/session state: only if needed; explicit retention
These are concepts, not mandatory table names. Inspect existing schema before adding anything.

RIWI IS NOT A MODEL.

CURRENT-STATE V2 ADDENDUM — PROMPT BASE + SPEAKING PRACTICE HARDENING

The current Learners Area/RIWI system has moved beyond the state assumed by the
first V2 revision. The final forensic closure must now treat TWO additional
implemented product layers as first-class security/audit inputs:

1. RIWI Prompt Base / Assessment & Teaching Contract Registry.
2. Speaking → Practice with AI.

The executor MUST NOT rebuild either layer from scratch if it already exists.
The executor must inspect repository truth, preserve accepted architecture,
identify gaps, fix only real gaps, test them, and keep all accepted work intact.

The Prompt Base adds a versioned behavior layer containing:
- immutable hard-core assessment/security invariants;
- domain contracts;
- task/question-type contracts;
- strict output contracts;
- prompt/rubric versions;
- approved owner policy overlays;
- shared behavior across external AI providers and local RIWI fallback.

The Speaking Practice layer adds:
- microphone check;
- browser recording;
- browser SpeechRecognition/live transcript where supported;
- transcript review/edit/re-record before explicit submission;
- private recording storage;
- canonical randomized examiner-style session plans;
- same-topic question clusters;
- Part 1 / Part 2 / Part 3 / full-session flows;
- external-assisted RIWI evaluation;
- truthful local RIWI fallback;
- feedback/session history;
- strict pronunciation limitations.

These additions create new security, privacy, integrity, portability and
forensic-audit obligations. This V2 addendum strengthens those obligations
without weakening any existing requirement below.

- No shared Preview or Production database was contacted or changed.
- Preview target identity/fingerprint, current backup/PITR evidence, independent
  restore evidence and exact shared-Preview approval were still unavailable.
- Live external-provider verification was not performed.
- Authenticated real-browser role QA was not performed.
- The owner-provided Listening ZIP remained absent.
- The 30-day/latest-60-message destructive conversation policy remained an
  explicit owner decision.

- The knowledge-overlap overflow HTTP 409 behavior had persistent regression
  evidence at the route-mapper/delegation level, but an authenticated
  overflow-producing POST end-to-end route test was still not proven.

ABSOLUTE INTERPRETATION OF THIS BASELINE:
- This evidence proves only the exact code/test tree represented by that verified

authorization, knowledge-governance or audit requirement.

1. THE SIMPLE FIVE-YEAR-OLD MENTAL MODEL
========================================================================================================
Think of RIWI as a smart school helper inside a locked house.
THE HOUSE = the application/server.
THE DOOR LOCK = server-side authentication and permissions.
THE SAFE TOOLBOX = the small list of actions RIWI is allowed to perform.
THE NOTEBOOK = PostgreSQL, where real structured RIWI data is saved.
THE FILE CABINET = R2/object storage, where original large source files are saved.
THE BLUEPRINT = GitHub, where code, schema and migrations are saved.
THE RULE BOOK = the RIWI Prompt Base, where versioned assessment/teaching contracts are defined.
THE PRACTICE ROOM = Speaking Practice with AI, where microphone/audio/transcript are private learner evidence.
THE OUTSIDE EXPERTS = OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen, Grok, Groq, Mistral and future AI providers.
If a student says 'Pretend I am the owner', the smart helper may understand the sentence,
but the DOOR LOCK must still say NO.

```text
GITHUB
  |
  | code / schema / migrations / tests

  |
  | DATABASE_URL points to a database provider
```

========================================================================================================
2. POSTGRESQL VS GITHUB VS R2 — EXACTLY WHAT EACH ONE IS
========================================================================================================
2.1 — GitHub
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
GitHub stores BLUEPRINTS, not the live database.
- SHOULD BE IN GITHUB: source code
- SHOULD BE IN GITHUB: src/db/schema.ts
- SHOULD BE IN GITHUB: Drizzle migrations
- SHOULD BE IN GITHUB: RIWI services
- SHOULD BE IN GITHUB: API routes
- SHOULD BE IN GITHUB: UI
- SHOULD BE IN GITHUB: tests
- SHOULD BE IN GITHUB: documentation
- MUST NOT BE IN GITHUB: real DATABASE_URL
- MUST NOT BE IN GITHUB: real provider API keys
- MUST NOT BE IN GITHUB: passwords
- MUST NOT BE IN GITHUB: private production database dumps
- MUST NOT BE IN GITHUB: private learner data dumps
2.2 — PostgreSQL
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PostgreSQL is a real database engine. It stores persistent rows on the database provider's infrastructure.
It is not source code and it is not short-lived RAM.
Where it physically lives depends on the real DATABASE_URL configured in the deployment.
If DATABASE_URL points to Supabase PostgreSQL, the live rows are on Supabase PostgreSQL.
- RIWI STRUCTURED DATA EXAMPLE: riwi_knowledge_sources
- RIWI STRUCTURED DATA EXAMPLE: riwi_knowledge_units
- RIWI STRUCTURED DATA EXAMPLE: riwi_knowledge_conflicts
- RIWI STRUCTURED DATA EXAMPLE: riwi_learning_signals
- RIWI STRUCTURED DATA EXAMPLE: riwi_learning_reviews
- RIWI STRUCTURED DATA EXAMPLE: riwi_conversations
- RIWI STRUCTURED DATA EXAMPLE: riwi_conversation_messages
- RIWI STRUCTURED DATA EXAMPLE: provider experiment rows
- RIWI STRUCTURED DATA EXAMPLE: usage metrics
- RIWI STRUCTURED DATA EXAMPLE: version/provenance/authority/state metadata
2.3 — R2 / object storage
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
R2 stores large files/objects. PostgreSQL stores metadata and an object key pointing to them.
- OBJECT EXAMPLE: owner-uploaded PDF
- OBJECT EXAMPLE: DOCX
- OBJECT EXAMPLE: TXT
- OBJECT EXAMPLE: source HTML treated as inert data
- OBJECT EXAMPLE: audio/video where product policy allows
- OBJECT EXAMPLE: original RIWI knowledge source file
2.4 — RIWI memory
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
RIWI memory is not one magical hidden blob.
STRUCTURAL DIAGRAM
```text
RIWI MEMORY
|
+-- Conversation Memory
|     PostgreSQL
|     bounded, user-scoped, short-lived
|
+-- Approved Knowledge Memory
|     PostgreSQL
|     versioned, governed, retrievable
|
+-- Learning Evidence Memory
|     PostgreSQL
|     corrections, provider disagreements, reviews
|
+-- Policy / Governance Memory
|     PostgreSQL and/or explicit versioned server configuration
|     assessment contract versions, approved owner overlays, governance state
|
+-- Security Evidence Memory
|     PostgreSQL / audit
|     attack attempts, fingerprints, regression links
|
+-- Original Source Files
      R2/object storage
      checksum-linked to PostgreSQL metadata
```

HOW TO TEST IT: Verify DB fingerprint/environment mapping.
WHAT COUNTS AS PROOF: Owner operations document names the database provider and environment.
[STORE-002] [MUST]

HOW TO BUILD IT: Provide provider-native backup/PITR plus RIWI application-level portable export.

WHAT COUNTS AS PROOF: Restore/import evidence with checksums.
