08. DEDICATED LISTENING MCQ — UNLIMITED NUMBER OF DAYS; FIVE REAL QUESTIONS PER DAY
====================================================================================================

THIS IS A NEW OWNER OVERRIDE WITH HIGH PRIORITY.

The current `src/lib/listening/mcq-program.ts` has the literal:
  export const MCQ_PROGRAM_DAY_TARGET = 30;
The old header/comment describes "30-day programme" and a "150 in total" target. Those values
ARE NOT A HARD PRODUCT LIMIT. The owner may publish Day 1…30, Day 1…100, Day 1…365, Day
1…1000 or any practical amount, then hide/archive old Days and upload new valid material.
Remove ANY arbitrary 30-day ceiling in constants, schema constraints, API/Zod validators,
editor/importer, program catalogue pagination, analytics, progress copy, tests, scripts, i18n,
seed fixtures, docs and staff preview. Discover all literal 30/150 references and classify
whether historical/example versus an operative product constraint.

OWNER RULES:
  * There is NO fixed maximum number of days and NO baked-in 150-question cap.
  * A day has a positive stable AUTHOR-ASSIGNED ordinal, not parsed from a display title.
  * Each PUBLISHED day still holds EXACTLY 5 authentic canonical MCQs in authored order.
  * Drafts can be incomplete; 4 or 6 question days cannot publish.
  * Show ONLY truly published real Days; missing Day 31 is NOT rendered as a fake card.
  * Support noncontiguous ordinals if old days were archived (unless an explicit product choice
    documented and owner-approved requires contiguous presentation). No implicit "unlock next".
  * Support hundreds/thousands of days using bounded server-side pagination and suitable indexes.
  * Existing `program_ref` and `program_ordinal` columns from migration 0052 must be reused.
    DO NOT rewrite migration 0052 or introduce a second MCQ schema merely to remove the cap.
  * `listening_mcq_sessions` remains the ONE learner-specific staged source of truth.
  * 5 question positions come from canonical authored questions; no content cloning.
  * Before stage reveal, official choices absent from actual API payload; key only after permitted
    stage. Listen -> learner prediction/notes -> commit -> reveal -> select -> reason -> result.
  * Day completed only after all FIVE are in genuine terminal reasoned stage.
  * Leave during Q3 committed -> return to Q3 committed with Q1/2 completed, not Q1 reset.
  * Academic/General MCQs NEVER join dedicated program automatically.
  * No IELTS band derived from five training MCQs.

CONTENT LIFE-CYCLE OVERRIDE: "remove old and upload new" is a legitimate admin use case.
Implement SAFE withdrawal/archival/replacement, NOT destructive cascades:
  - Staff can unpublish/archive an existing Day. It disappears from NEW learner catalogue.
  - Completed/in-progress personal session history and auditable authored source/version remain
    recoverable under an explicit, authorized history policy; never silently reuse old question
    UUIDs with new answers, audio or semantics.
  - Replacing Day 8 with new content does not mutate a finished old Day 8 session into a new quiz.
  - Decide duplicate ordinal/reuse based on existing uniqueness/versioning constraints; use new
    immutable version/identity or controlled archival semantics. If 0052 unique index prevents
    archival+replacement with same ordinal, prove smallest safe additive migration needed (0053
    only with upgrade plan and owner approval), not a dangerous workaround.
  - Hard deletion is forbidden for content with linked attempts/sessions unless formally approved
    deletion/retention policy says otherwise. Do NOT cascade-delete real learner history.
  - Archive/restore and staff deletion confirmation are permission-gated and auditable.
  - If an item without history can be permanently deleted, follow existing policy and test FK
    restrictions/rollback. Never implement "delete everything then reimport" to update Days.
  - Import duplicate detection, idempotency, source provenance/checksums, ordinal collision
    responses, version identity and staff preview are first-class.

EXAMPLES THAT MUST PASS:
  A: Owner publishes 100 Days × 5 = 500 real MCQs. Days 1, 30, 31, 99, 100 all accessible;
     day ordering and total count correct, page reads bounded, not 100 cards at once.
  B: Only Days 1, 2 and 100 published. Learner sees those three, NO fake Day 3–99.
  C: Day 30 is archived. Existing learner history stays intact; NEW catalogue omits Day 30.
  D: Staff publishes a new authored day safely after old content archived; old learner answers
     remain tied to the old immutable question set.
  E: Import of 100 days contains one invalid Day 74 (four MCQs). Publication of 74 is refused
     with exact actionable reason; rest only proceeds under accepted transactional policy.
  F: 4, 6, duplicate positions, duplicate source keys, Matching/Map, absent audio/keys:
     publish refused; no fifth question or audio fabricated.
  G: Student A Day 100 progress never appears for Student B. API tampering returns 403/404.
  H: Page refresh/back/deep link of an archived/current Day follows the real visibility/history
     contract and never exposes an unpublished question key.

SEARCH EVERY HARD-CODED ASSUMPTION, INCLUDING:
  MCQ_PROGRAM_DAY_TARGET, "30-day", "30 days", "150", day >= 30, day <= 30,
  length <= 30, pagination fixed to 30, ordinal validation, Zod `.max(30)`, UI translation,
  import templates, seed limits, programme completion denominators and release reports.

If target-size metadata is useful, make it OPTIONAL staff-authored planning metadata, not a
publication gate, learner-visible fake target or code limit. Existing users must not lose days.

  FIRST USE (entry -> actual action -> saved result/review)
  RELOAD/RESUME (correct place and state)
  TWO TABS / RACE (server writes coherent)
  CROSS-USER/TAMPER (refuse)
  PUBLISHED/DRAFT/ARCHIVED (correct visibility)
  NETWORK LOSS / TIMEOUT (truthful recovery)
  KEYBOARD / TOUCH / MOBILE (actual user can interact)
  LOCALIZATION (EN/UZ)
  CLEANUP (no fixture residue; no unrelated deletion).

Actual audio recording needs microphone permission/hardware or an explicitly named simulator;
actual real audio playback/quality cannot be claimed solely from jsdom. External AI/provider or
R2 credentials may require owner access; mark those UNVERIFIED rather than PASS if unavailable.

====================================================================================================
24. FINAL TWO-PASS FORENSIC AUDIT — THE CORE OWNER REQUIREMENT
====================================================================================================

PASS 1: Requirement-by-requirement THIRD-PERSON AUDIT after EACH implementation checkpoint.
As reviewer ask:
  “If I had not seen the implementation, does the final product prove the promised behavior?”
  “Can a user actually complete the task using visible buttons?”
  “Can another student/role exploit this?”
  “Are keys/private notes inadvertently sent to browser?”
  “What happens to historical data when staff revises/deletes an item?”
  “Does the last action show truth, not success-colored optimism?”
  “Are mobile/keyboard paths real?”
  “What is the next smallest test that could falsify this?”
Write and execute that test. Fix root cause; rerun regressions; push only stable checkpoint.

PASS 2: WHOLE-WEBSITE INDEPENDENT FORENSIC AUDIT after all checkpoints are coded.
Use the entire actual navigation/action/role matrix from a FRESH build. Revisit untouched modules
and cross-module contracts. Review EVERY newly added file and dependent unchanged file. Include
DB constraints, migrations, RBAC, unsafe import, performance, accessibility, responsiveness,
privacy, R2/binary integrity, active exam secrecy, scheduled content, archive and old history.
Construct fresh independent fixtures DIFFERENT from original developer tests and real browser
user journeys. DO NOT begin by repeating only pass-1 exact expected snapshots.

Upon finding ANY P0/P1:
  - capture reproducible exact failing route/action/role/data/SHA
  - add a regression test proving failure
  - patch minimal production root cause without weakening security
  - rerun focused + cross-module tests
  - run another full frozen-tree gate and repeat pass-2 affected checks
  - push commit, verify remote, recheck Vercel.

Completion requires two clean audits, not just one post-implementation test run.

25. FULL FROZEN QUALITY GATE — EXACT COMMANDS AND INTERPRETATION
====================================================================================================

Once implementation is complete, FREEZE the actual tree and run:
  npm ci                # only if dependencies missing/lockfile changed; never fake pass
  npm run typecheck
  npm run lint
  npm run build
  git diff --check
  npm test
  npm run test:ui
  npm run qa:pg
  npm run qa:gate

Add route/built-server/real Chromium acceptance, app-wide user-role matrix, MCQ 100-day scenario,
history-retention regression, Content OS authoring/publish race, cross-module and security
negative cases. Execute fresh-install and accepted-state upgrade if schema changed.

For EACH suite capture EXACT total / pass / fail / skip, command, environment class, exit code,
SHA, timestamp, fixture ownership and reproducible evidence path. Do not sum overlapping suites
and claim combined unique test count. Skip is NOT pass. A missing owner asset may justify an
explicit SKIPPED/OWNER DEPENDENCY but cannot justify claiming complete source publication.

IMPORTANT: 0 lint errors, 0 type errors, 0 build errors, diff checks, full gate pass, and zero
unresolved reproduced repo-solvable P0/P1 are MINIMUMS, not substitutes for real UX acceptance.
If a code/test change occurs after gate, the gate is stale: re-run on the new frozen tree.
Documentation-only commit does not change gated code, but prove it is docs-only.

28. CONCRETE RELEASE SCENARIOS — FULL SYSTEM GOLDEN JOURNEYS
====================================================================================================

GOLDEN-01 Dashboard: student logs in, opens dashboard, uses Continue, saves work, returns and
sees actual progress; another student sees only their own.
GOLDEN-02 Listening Academic: published actual 4x40 test -> hub -> active safe exam -> submit
-> review evidence -> retry real misses; audio lifecycle correct; no key before submit.
GOLDEN-03 General Listening: section -> audio/questions -> temporary attempt notes/highlight
-> submit -> own section result; no Academic activity hub; no cross-user state.
GOLDEN-04 MCQ 100 days: staff imports/publishes 100 valid ordered days; student loads page 1,
next page, opens Day 100, stops at Q3 committed and resumes; fifth reasoned completes;
student B remains 0/5. Pagination SQL bounded, NO day >=31 rejection or 150 cap.
GOLDEN-05 MCQ archive/replace: staff archives Day 8 with a learner's prior session; new learner
catalogue hides it; authorized learner old history remains valid, new Day 8 source never rewrites
old answers; duplicate ordinal/race errors clear and reversible.
GOLDEN-06 Reading Academic: genuine 3x40 -> timed full attempt -> highlight w/o Dictionary ->
autosave reload -> submit -> own post-submit evidence/explanation/Dictionary; v1 history stable
across v2 publication.
GOLDEN-07 Reading General: Passage 2, highlighting + Dictionary together, autosave, Check,
authored explanation; FULL shows 3 actual passages, not a fake fourth one.
GOLDEN-08 Reading Question Types + Retention: canonical type -> bounded real passage index ->
canonical practice; direct Retention -> timed recall -> own graded result/history.
GOLDEN-09 TED: summary text save; record local voice, listen, re-record, switch internal tabs;
leave to Reading; return -> written text still present, audio gone; network sees NO audio upload.
GOLDEN-10 Writing: real prompt -> draft/save -> submit -> legitimate feedback/review; old prompt
revision preserves history and no RIWI side edits performed.
GOLDEN-11 Speaking: real prompt -> microphone permission -> record/playback/retry, valid own attempt
where supported; cleanup tracks on leaving.
GOLDEN-12 Vocabulary: contextual word lookup/sense disambiguation -> save -> folder/SRS;
reuse same lexeme from another module, no duplicate meaning guess.
GOLDEN-13 Grammar: authored topic -> practice -> check/review -> own progress; source revision
must not rewrite another student's completed result.
GOLDEN-14 Live class/assignment: authorized scheduled item -> student participate/submit ->
teacher/owner see only proper roster/submission; invalid or inaccessible links fail truthfully.
GOLDEN-15 Staff Content OS: draft -> validate/preview -> published v1 -> learner attempt ->
published v2 -> old attempt retains v1 -> archive -> history available.
GOLDEN-16 Security: anonymous/suspended/other-student requests and tampered IDs rejected at SSR
and API layer, including attempts, answers, private notes, source assets and reports.
GOLDEN-17 Device/I18N: 320/375/390/430/768/1024/1440 desktop/mobile routes, keyboard/touch,
no hidden controls, UZ/EN copy correct; theme CSS/visual styling unchanged by Arena.
GOLDEN-18 Operations: fresh install migrations, accepted-state upgrade if changed, real-PG suite,
preview deploy for final SHA, safe teardown/rollback evidence, clean Git.

A scenario PASSES only when a real test/probe/browser exercise with named fixture proves the
entire journey and cleanup, not because a screenshot resembles the desired screen.
